Done. Reflection summary:

This wasn't a reasoning error — my computed answer [44.00, 231.52] was numerically identical to the gold [44.00,231.52]. The only difference was a space after the comma. The grader is whitespace-strict, so a perfect answer got marked WRONG purely on formatting.

This is highly generalizable (it would silently fail every otherwise-correct multi-value answer), so I:
- Updated memory's format rule to flag the no-space-after-comma requirement with this exact worked example.
- Fixed the skill's "Output format" section, which was actively wrong (it said "comma + space separated") — now it mandates bare commas `[v1,v2,v3]` and keeping trailing zeros, plus added two items to the pitfalls checklist.

The inflation-adjustment methodology itself (CPI-U deflation to a base month, then linear regression slope/intercept) was correct and is adequately covered by existing stats-wrapper patterns, so nothing new to save there.
